gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Synology's own DS925+ page withholds 'complete product warranty or technical support' if non-Synology memory is installed and requires identical modules, or that QNAP's TS-464 spec page caps RAM at 16 GB (2 × 8 GB, QNAP modules with identical specs) and runs both M.2 slots at PCIe Gen 3 x1 and the expansion slot at Gen 3 x2.
standout_why: I compared against Starry Hope's Synology Alternatives and Best 4-Bay NAS pages (both cited), nasdrives.ca (cited) and our own current page. Starry Hope gives the DS925+ 32 GB maximum, says the DS925+ M.2 slots accept only Synology-listed NVMe drives, gives the DXP4800 Plus 64 GB and 2× PCIe 4.0 M.2, and says the TS-464 has a 'PCIe slot that takes a 10GbE or faster network card'. None of these pages state Synology's warranty and support clause for third-party RAM, the TS-464's 16 GB ceiling and QNAP module advice, or the TS-464's Gen 3 x1 M.2 and Gen 3 x2 slot widths. None of them, ours included, mentions UPS pairing at all. I could not read thisping.com because of a certificate error.
decides: It supports the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus as the pick for a home user who will add RAM or NVMe. Synology ties a DS925+ RAM upgrade to Synology modules if the owner wants full warranty and support, and still restricts M.2 pools to Synology-verified SSDs. QNAP's TS-464, the 'mature alternative', stops at 16 GB and its M.2 slots get one Gen 3 lane each. It does not make the TS-464 a worse pick for someone who wants to add a 10GbE card later, because the Gen 3 x2 slot is enough for that.

findings.label: Memory rule and third-party RAM warranty
findings.value: 4 GB DDR4 ECC SODIMM installed, 32 GB maximum (16 GB × 2), 2 slots; 'all modules must be identical and share the same model number'; Synology will not provide 'complete product warranty or technical support if non-Synology memory modules are used'
findings.source_title: DS925+ | Synology Inc. (US product page, specs)
findings.note: Maker's US product page, specs footnotes.

findings.label: M.2 NVMe pools
findings.value: 2 × M.2 2280 NVMe for cache or storage pools; 'Creating M.2 storage pools requires the use of Synology-verified SSDs'; SSD cache needs select compatible SSDs; M.2 not hot-swappable
findings.source_title: DS925+ | Synology Inc. (US product page, specs)
findings.note: Starry Hope already states this, so it is not new. Included to fill the table cell.

findings.label: Variant: DS925neo+
findings.value: The same spec page lists a DS925neo+ with 4 GB non-ECC SODIMM where the DS925+ has ECC; both have a 32 GB maximum
findings.source_title: DS925+ | Synology Inc. (US product page, specs)
findings.note: No rival page or ChatGPT answer mentions the neo+ variant. I did not check its price or US availability.

findings.label: Expansion port and warranty
findings.value: 2 × USB 3.2 Gen 1 plus 1 USB Type-C expansion port; 3-year warranty, extendable to 5 years with Extended Warranty Plus (Europe and North America only)
findings.source_title: DS925+ | Synology Inc. (US product page, specs)
findings.note: The page did not name the expansion unit model on this read.

findings.label: Memory limit and module rule
findings.value: 8 GB DDR4 SODIMM installed, 16 GB maximum (2 × 8 GB), 2 slots; for dual-DIMM setups use 'QNAP modules with identical specifications'
findings.note: Maker's US hardware spec page. The legacy TS-464-4G ships with 4 GB.

findings.label: M.2 and PCIe slot bandwidth
findings.value: 2 × M.2 2280 at PCIe Gen 3 x1 (not hot-swappable; heatsink under 68 × 20 × 10 mm); 1 × PCIe Gen 3 x2 slot, card up to 190 × 68.9 × 18.76 mm; 5GbE/10GbE only through an optional PCIe card
findings.note: Gen 3 is about 1 GB/s per lane, so each M.2 slot tops out near 1 GB/s and the x2 slot near 2 GB/s, which is enough for one 10GbE port (about 1.25 GB/s). The page lists QM2/QXG/QXP cards as optional but the per-model compatibility list did not load.

findings.label: Warranty split
findings.value: 3-year standard warranty; bundled accessories such as expansion cards and the power adapter carry 1 year

findings.label: Model exclusions and output
findings.value: 120 W maximum output, 43.2 Wh battery, USB data link to the NAS; Notebookcheck says it works 'only with some of the company's NAS models' and does not support the DXP6800 and DXP8800 series; about $100 at launch
findings.source_title: Notebookcheck: Compact UPS protects data integrity and ensures round-the-clock availability of NAS (2025-10-06)
findings.note: Named reviewer as a fallback because UGREEN's product page returned HTTP 429 on 4 tries. Notebookcheck does not list the DXP4800 Plus by name, so the positive pairing is still unsourced. The price is a 2025 launch figure, not today's.

findings.label: US3000 UPS signalling under a third-party OS
findings.value: A NASCompares reader running TrueNAS on a DXP4800 Plus reported upsc 'Error: Driver not connected' although lsusb showed the US3000; NASCompares' guide adds a manual NUT/udev setup (vendor 2b89, product ffff, usbhid-ups) to make the US3000 work on a TerraMaster F4-424 Pro
findings.source_title: NASCompares: How to Make the UGREEN US3000 NAS UPS Work on a TerraMaster F4-424 Pro (2025-09-29; reader comment 2026-01-12)
findings.note: Single reader comment, so anecdotal; label it that way if used. The workaround is NASCompares' own and not supported by UGREEN.

findings.label: RAM ceiling and NVMe policy (named reviewer)
findings.value: 8 GB DDR5, up to 64 GB over two slots; 'no drive compatibility list: any SATA drive or NVMe SSD works'; 2 × PCIe 4.0 M.2
findings.source_title: Starry Hope: Best 4-Bay NAS in 2026 for Home and Office
findings.note: This is a rival's statement, used as the comparison column. UGREEN's own pages returned 429, so the maker figure is unconfirmed.
